skip_reason: Existing-move logistics call, not a sales call. Teju Onabajo had already booked a move for Saturday Sept 12 (quoted by Jillian) and called to shift the arrival window from morning to afternoon because of his building's elevator reservation. The call is a schedule change plus follow-up questions on TV protection, keeping moving blankets in storage, and the packing-supply rate. No quoting, no pricing pitch, no booking attempt — nothing the 85-point scorecard is built to measure.
top_strength: Answered three unrelated follow-up questions cleanly and without deflecting — the TV-bag size limit ('either way we do have a process for protecting and moving TVs no matter the size'), the blanket buy-back ('bring them back to us and we'll give you a full refund for what you paid for them'), and the $189 supply estimate, which he correctly framed as an average bundle and volunteered would likely come in under. Customer closed with 'no questions, this has been helpful, thank you.'
coaching_note: LIVE BUSINESS RISK, not a scoring issue. Jillian's estimate on this booked move is eight and a half hours. Garrison moved the arrival window to the afternoon at the customer's request, which cuts available crew time to about five hours against a 6:30 hard stop — and he said out loud that Jillian 'seems to believe... we may not be able to knock this out within five,' then booked it anyway and later widened it again to an 11:00-1:00 window. Either the eight-and-a-half-hour estimate is wrong (the customer thinks it is — he's packing his own clothes and it's a one-bedroom) or we are knowingly setting a crew up to run out of clock on a move where the customer's own elevator reservation ends. Somebody should re-scope this before Sept 12 rather than let it land on the crew. Two smaller items: the new window and the supply-cost breakdown were both promised by email and need to actually be updated in EMMA, not just verbally agreed; and he twice stated the window as '12:00 AM to 2:00 PM' — likely a transcript artifact or a slip, but the customer heard it and it should read 12:00 PM. He also never used the customer's name.
phone_presence_notes: Accommodating and clear under a customer-driven schedule change, flexed twice without friction and the customer volunteered that the call was helpful — short of a 5 on no name use and on letting the eight-and-a-half-versus-five-hour contradiction sit unresolved.
